newsletter.title: This week in clones: Creative suites get cloned, and the hype keeps climbing
newsletter.intro: This week saw a wide spread of clones, from AI video studios to full office and photo suites. Several projects are now rated Loved by both X and GitHub, while a larger group of new announcements sits at Hyped, unproven until more people weigh in.
newsletter.outro: Next week we will see whether the Hyped, unproven projects hold up once more people have tried them.

items.name: Open-Generative-AI
items.blurb: Open-Generative-AI, a clone of OpenAI Sora, is rated Loved with 45 likes across 4 posts and 31900 stars on GitHub. It is pitched as a free AI video studio with 600+ models and no subscription.

items.name: CCleaner, CleanMyMac clone
items.blurb: The CCleaner, CleanMyMac clone is rated Hyped, unproven on 430 likes from a single post. It is a free, open-source Mac and Windows cleaner built by reverse-engineering the two apps with Claude.

items.name: WordCraft
items.blurb: WordCraft, a clone of Microsoft Word, is rated Loved with 86 likes across 4 posts and 16768 stars on GitHub. It is a clean-room open-source reimplementation written in pure Rust.

items.name: Content Studio
items.blurb: Content Studio, a clone of Canva, is rated Hyped, unproven on 242 likes from one post. It is an open-source Slack design agent that makes on-brand videos, graphics, and decks.

items.name: PhotoCraft
items.blurb: PhotoCraft, a clone of Adobe Photoshop, is rated Loved with 210 likes across 30 posts and 75319 stars on GitHub. It is an open-source project by storytold that reproduces the look and features of Photoshop and Illustrator.

items.name: Revideo
items.blurb: Revideo moved from Loved to Hyped, unproven this week. It is a free open-source alternative to the paid Revid content creation tool, and it drew 87 likes from one post.

items.name: ArtCraft
items.blurb: ArtCraft is rated Loved with 1565 likes across 39 posts and 37889 stars on GitHub. It is a vibe-coded set of open-source Rust replacements for seven of Adobe's apps, making it the most-discussed project of the week.

items.name: e2e
items.blurb: The e2e project is rated Loved with 205 likes from one post and 12360 stars on GitHub. The author says 21 parallel Claude agents reverse engineered an unnamed product, and the result was released as free open-source code.

items.name: BimCraft
items.blurb: BimCraft, a clone of Revit, moved from Mixed to Hyped, unproven. It is a free, open-source, vibe-coded alpha BIM authoring app that uses IFC as its native format.

items.name: Higgsfield clone
items.blurb: The Higgsfield clone is rated Hyped, unproven on 50 likes from one post. The author reverse engineered the Higgsfield app, including its Genjutsu feature, and offers a version about 30% cheaper on average.

items.name: Discord clone
items.blurb: The Discord clone is rated Hyped, unproven on 89 likes from one post. The author announced an open-source alternative to Discord with limited invite slots.

items.name: subvox
items.blurb: subvox moved from Mixed to Hyped, unproven on 1697 likes from one post. The author recreated the subvocal app for AirPods Pro 3 in nine minutes using a single prompt.

results.text:
Show HN: OpenArcanum – An End-to-End Encrypted Alternative to Discord
A while back I recall being told it can't be done and won't be "Discord". To that, I have to admit, it's not Discord. It isn't designed in a way to profile it's users and it respects privacy. There is still much work to do on this project, but it's in open beta with a web client so people can see how it works before committing to a desktop app download. Mobile apps will come later, if there is proven interest in this platform. I don't care to monitize it. The only thing users will ever see is a non-intrusive "Please donate" badge at most, with the intentions to just keep the maintainer nodes and some official relays running. There are no accounts. There is no way for me to see the messages. It is a platform that respects the user's privacy and asks nothing of it's user's. Anyone can run the entire stack in their own hardware, in private, with no limitations on controlling their data. It is open source (AGPLv3: https://github.com/hyperkubeorg/openarcanum/ And it's live right now for you to check out: https://openarcanum.org I have a community server running that you may join with this community code (good for 30 days): ``` openarcanum-invite:ChACbbppkdJgXT5JFDYAyCMdEiBcigeLKcJMz5_6LKRhT_sSlYXITfl7Mctu2I5hRPmT1hogy8dDt7EjO6KG5Xz-ufvsCFWE8f_yQtaCFFYE8M83UcEiIXdzczovL3JlbGF5LTAxLm9wZW5hcmNhbnVtLm9yZy93cyIhd3NzOi8vcmVsYXktMDIub3BlbmFyY2FudW0ub3JnL3dzKhhBMnJXa1BYRGRkbHVsVC13V1ZTbDg2OHcyEEhhY2tlciBOZXdzIENyZXc ```

Show HN: Wanim – Manim in the browser, but 1/20 smaller
Hi HN, I really like Manim, but when I tried to use it to make interactive small demos on the web, I found that no project can simultaneously satisfy running original manim python code without carrying the bulky pyodide which makes it impossible to embed. So I made one. My idea is to rewrite a js library that is almost completely identical to manim, and then patch rapydscript-ng to translate the original code to js, and support numpy syntax. It looks surprisingly good, supports the vast majority of syntax, and the size is only about 1M (1/20 of pyodide)! You can try it at https://wanim.org/playground , and there is an interactive courseware example at https://wanim.org/blog .
https://github.com/Acfboy/Wanim

Show HN: HackerFlow – A Responsive HN Reader
A lot of people love hacker news because the website is simple, fast, and its UI stays out of the way. I just can't seem to leave well enough alone I built HackerFlow because I wanted to browse HN visually while keeping articles and comments in the same place.The goal is a fast UI that stays out of the way but offers more visuals. I tried a few other GUIs and none of them really satisfied me. Features: - Gallery, magazine, list and compact views - Inline article reader with rendered text and page previews - Infinite scrolling with thumbnail preloading - Collapsible comments, capped indentation and next-parent navigation - Preserved scroll position when opening stories or navigating back - Search, local bookmarks, dark mode and keyboard shortcuts - Responsive layouts and an installable web app - Bookmarked articles stored in your browser no monetization, no accounts.
https://hn.vinceroyer.ca/

results.text:
Show HN: Balk – A Baseball Game
Balk is a baseball game. Things like MLB Showdown and other baseball games captured my attention growing up, but never really filled the void of a game. They were fun to look at and scheme, but the game itself was missing something. I think baseball lends itself really well to game design. There are a lot of games that exist inside the game of baseball. It’s a deeply flawed and broken sport, but so are humans, and in some ways that makes baseball better. It’s baseball. You already know the rules, and that’s the point. You play against another person, or against Tin Pete, the bot. A game takes about 30 minutes, honestly I’m not sure, I can play it fast but I’m using the hotkeys. It’s what I’d consider alpha, and I’m still trying to find what’s fun. It’s been a nice outlet and a break from solving business problems, though the same skill set gets invoked: distill a complex idea down to its most basic implementation. Stack is Java, React, Postgres, on a $5 Digital Ocean instance. I'm sure you can bring it down if you are bored. There’s some slop TOS and privacy policy up. No trackers, nothing sold. Happy to update the intention was that these were easy to understand and I'm not interested in selling your data. If you want to see how it was built, day by day, counted from the repo: https://balk.club/blog/timeline.html
https://balk.club

groups.text:
Show HN: OpenArcanum – An End-to-End Encrypted Alternative to Discord
A while back I recall being told it can't be done and won't be "Discord". To that, I have to admit, it's not Discord. It isn't designed in a way to profile it's users and it respects privacy. There is still much work to do on this project, but it's in open beta with a web client so people can see how it works before committing to a desktop app download. Mobile apps will come later, if there is proven interest in this platform. I don't care to monitize it. The only thing users will ever see is a non-intrusive "Please donate" badge at most, with the intentions to just keep the maintainer nodes and some official relays running. There are no accounts. There is no way for me to see the messages. It is a platform that respects the user's privacy and asks nothing of it's user's. Anyone can run the entire stack in their own hardware, in private, with no limitations on controlling their data. It is open source (AGPLv3: https://github.com/hyperkubeorg/openarcanum/ And it's live right now for you to check out: https://openarcanum.org I have a community server running that you may join with this community code (good for 30 days): ``` openarcanum-invite:ChACbbppkdJgXT5JFDYAyCMdEiBcigeLKcJMz5_6LKRhT_sSlYXITfl7Mctu2I5hRPmT1hogy8dDt7EjO6KG5Xz-ufvsCFWE8f_yQtaCFFYE8M83UcEiIXdzczovL3JlbGF5LTAxLm9wZW5hcmNhbnVtLm9yZy93cyIhd3NzOi8vcmVsYXktMDIub3BlbmFyY2FudW0ub3JnL3dzKhhBMnJXa1BYRGRkbHVsVC13V1ZTbDg2OHcyEEhhY2tlciBOZXdzIENyZXc ```

Show HN: Wanim – Manim in the browser, but 1/20 smaller
Hi HN, I really like Manim, but when I tried to use it to make interactive small demos on the web, I found that no project can simultaneously satisfy running original manim python code without carrying the bulky pyodide which makes it impossible to embed. So I made one. My idea is to rewrite a js library that is almost completely identical to manim, and then patch rapydscript-ng to translate the original code to js, and support numpy syntax. It looks surprisingly good, supports the vast majority of syntax, and the size is only about 1M (1/20 of pyodide)! You can try it at https://wanim.org/playground , and there is an interactive courseware example at https://wanim.org/blog .

Show HN: Balk – A Baseball Game
Balk is a baseball game. Things like MLB Showdown and other baseball games captured my attention growing up, but never really filled the void of a game. They were fun to look at and scheme, but the game itself was missing something. I think baseball lends itself really well to game design. There are a lot of games that exist inside the game of baseball. It’s a deeply flawed and broken sport, but so are humans, and in some ways that makes baseball better. It’s baseball. You already know the rules, and that’s the point. You play against another person, or against Tin Pete, the bot. A game takes about 30 minutes, honestly I’m not sure, I can play it fast but I’m using the hotkeys. It’s what I’d consider alpha, and I’m still trying to find what’s fun. It’s been a nice outlet and a break from solving business problems, though the same skill set gets invoked: distill a complex idea down to its most basic implementation. Stack is Java, React, Postgres, on a $5 Digital Ocean instance. I'm sure you can bring it down if you are bored. There’s some slop TOS and privacy policy up. No trackers, nothing sold. Happy to update the intention was that these were easy to understand and I'm not interested in selling your data. If you want to see how it was built, day by day, counted from the repo: https://balk.club/blog/timeline.html
https://balk.club
